claimMap.claim: The House passed H.R. 9340 by 417–3 on September 16.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: The U.S. House passed H.R. 9340, the Ratepayer Protection Act, by 417–3 on September 16.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Vote Question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended
The Ratepayer Protection Act passed the U.S. House of Representatives on Sept. 16, 2026, by an overwhelming, bipartisan vote of 417-3.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Official House roll-call record and a Senate sponsor participant account checked September 23; House passage is not enactment.

claimMap.claim: The proposed standard covers specified non-residential computing facilities with peak demand of 100 megawatts or more at one site or campus.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: a covered non-residential computing or data facility with peak demand of at least 100 megawatts at one site or campus.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: have, in the aggregate, a peak electric demand of 100 megawatts or more at a single site or campus.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: House-engrossed definition checked September 23; not an enacted definition.

claimMap.claim: The proposed standard says a qualifying customer rate would recover the full incremental upgrade cost and require financial assurance before the upgrade.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: its rate would be designed to recover the full “incremental cost” — the additional grid-upgrade cost needed to serve that particular large customer. The customer would also provide financial assurance before construction.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: A rate charged, or entered into, by an electric utility for providing electric service to a large-load customer shall be designed to recover from the large-load customer the full, incremental cost of any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade necessary to serve the load of such large-load customer

Before making any generation, transmission, or distribution upgrade that is necessary to serve the load of a large-load customer, an electric utility shall require the large-load customer provide to the electric utility financial assurances or contributions to cover the cost of such upgrade.

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: Would apply only if enacted and through the applicable state or nonregulated-utility process.

claimMap.claim: If enacted, authorities would begin consideration within one year and complete consideration and make a determination within two.

candidateEvidence.excerpt: begin consideration or set a hearing within one year, then complete it and make a determination within two.

sourceEvidence.excerpt: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this paragraph, each State regulatory authority (with respect to each electric utility for which the State has ratemaking authority) and each nonregulated electric utility shall commence consideration under section 111, or set a hearing date for consideration, with respect to the standard

Not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this paragraph, each State regulatory authority (with respect to each electric utility for which the State has ratemaking authority) and each nonregulated electric utility shall complete the consideration and make the determination under section 111 with respect to the standard

claimMap.scopeAndFreshness: The federal obligation is consideration and determination; the House text does not itself set every local rate.
